m2c/tests/conftest.py -- Patch C01: shared fixtures.

Two jobs:

1. Hermeticity.  The autouse ``_hermetic_env`` fixture points both
   ``M2C_HOME`` and ``HOME`` at a per-test temp directory and clears
   ``M2C_LOG_LEVEL``, so no test can read or create anything in the real
   ``~/.m2c`` -- even a test that deliberately exercises the "M2C_HOME
   unset" fallback only ever sees the temp HOME.

2. A ``make_env`` factory that builds a ``doctor.Environment`` in which
   every probe is a plain value or a fake callable.  The doctor takes its
   facts through that one object (see m2c/doctor.py), so each check can be
   mocked individually without monkeypatching globals.

files.module_doc:
m2c/tests/test_checkpoints.py -- Patch C08: checkpoints and rewind.

A bug in this module can destroy the user's files, so most of what is here is
a failure path: corrupt blobs, symlinks swapped in after the snapshot, paths
that try to leave the project, an index that was edited by hand, a snapshot or
a rewind that is interrupted half way.  The happy path comes first and is
short: edit, edit, rewind, and the bytes are exactly what they were.

Fault injection
---------------
Two small, private functions of ``m2c.checkpoints`` are replaced by tests as
seams, because there is no other way to make a real failure land at exactly
that point:

* ``_insert_rows``  -- the one database transaction that records a step; a
  test makes it fail (or stall, in tests/test_checkpoints_crash.py) *after*
  every blob has been written and *before* any row is.
* ``_apply_item``   -- restores or deletes one file during a rewind; a test
  makes it fail after the first file.

The failure in the *middle* of the transaction needs no seam: it is a
database trigger that aborts the insert of one particular path.

Nothing here looks like a secret: file contents are random bytes or short
marker words, and every hash is computed at run time.

files.module_doc:
m2c/tests/test_checkpoints_crash.py -- Patch C08: a process that is killed in
the middle of a snapshot or a rewind.

tests/test_checkpoints.py injects failures inside one process.  That proves the
rollback paths; it cannot prove what a SIGKILL leaves on disk, because nothing
runs after one: no ``finally``, no ``atexit``, no rollback, no temp-file
clean-up.  So here a real child process is stopped at the interesting moment
and killed, and this process then looks at what is left.

* ``test_kill_after_the_blobs_before_the_index``: the child has written every
  blob and is about to open the index transaction.  After the kill: the
  database is healthy, the step has no rows at all (not even a partial set),
  the orphan blobs are there and harmless, the same step can be recorded again,
  and ``gc_orphans`` clears the orphans.
* ``test_kill_in_the_middle_of_a_rewind``: the child has restored one file and
  dies.  After the kill, running the same rewind in this process finishes the
  job and ends in exactly the state a clean rewind would have.

The kill points use the same two seams as the in-process tests
(``_insert_rows`` and ``_apply_item``), set inside the child, so no test hook
exists in the production code path.

files.module_doc:
m2c/tests/test_logging_setup.py -- Patch C01: "logging never records message
content".

The rule (build plan §11.4 applied to the client): nothing a user typed, a
model produced, or a tool returned may end up in a log line.  These tests
prove it for every route a value can take into a log record:

  * a field passed to log_event()                    (allowlist)
  * a %-style argument                               (args are redacted)
  * an ``extra=`` attribute                          (non-standard attrs removed)
  * an exception message in a traceback              (type name only)
  * a non-string object passed as the message        (suppressed)
  * a record already formatted by another handler    (exc_text cache)

and finish with an end-to-end canary: the real CLI runs ``doctor`` at DEBUG
level, with a secret in the project path, and the secret must not appear.

files.module_doc:
m2c/tests/test_store_crash.py -- Patch C02: an interrupted write leaves a
valid database.

Each test starts a real child process that talks to the store and kills it
with SIGKILL -- no ``finally``, no ``atexit``, no chance to roll back or
close the connection -- then reopens the database in this process.

* ``test_kill_with_an_open_uncommitted_transaction``: the child begins a
  transaction and writes enough that SQLite spills uncommitted pages to the
  WAL file; after the kill, ``PRAGMA integrity_check`` is ``ok`` and none of
  those rows is visible.
* ``test_kill_in_the_middle_of_a_stream_of_commits``: the child commits
  events one by one and reports each seq on stdout *after* the commit
  returned; after the kill, every reported seq is present and the log has no
  gaps.  (SIGKILL does not lose data the kernel already has, so an
  acknowledged commit must survive; power loss is what ``synchronous=FULL``
  is for and cannot be simulated here.)

Covers where the database lives (through paths.py, honouring M2C_HOME), the
file modes (0700 directory, 0600 database and its -wal / -shm sidecars,

interrupted write safe, the ``transaction()`` helper, and the promise that
nothing in the store touches the network.

m2c/tests/test_store_migrations.py -- Patch C02: the schema and its
forward-only migrations.

Two kinds of migration test live here:

* against the real ``MIGRATIONS`` list -- version 0 to latest, and every
  pair of versions in it -- so a migration added by a later patch is covered
  the moment it is appended;
* against a *synthetic* list (the real v1 plus two throwaway migrations), so
  the "between each pair of versions", "already migrated is left alone",
  "newer database", "failed migration rolls back" and "two processes race"
  behaviours are exercised today, while the real list has a single entry.
